title: Dilution, ventilation and exposure controls
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and apply: dilution, ventilation and exposure controls

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body:
Learning goal and job context: This lesson teaches dilution, ventilation and exposure controls for routine cleaning work. Start with the actual job scope, site instructions, manufacturer directions and worker training. Never treat a general lesson as authority to perform restricted or specialist work.

Core procedure: Read the manufacturer’s dilution instructions and use a dedicated labelled measuring system. Never estimate concentration by colour or smell. Assess ventilation, splashing, aerosols and people nearby before application. Use the PPE specified for the product and task; a stronger mix is not automatically more effective.

Decision-making in the field: Before acting, ask: What is the surface or equipment? What is the soil or hazard? Which product or method is approved? What could harm a person, property or food? If the answer is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.

Worked workplace scenario: An employee proposes doubling concentrate for a heavily soiled floor. The supervisor redirects them to the approved dilution and a repeat mechanical-cleaning step.

Guided supervised practice: Using water and a harmless training concentrate, calculate and demonstrate a labelled dilution, record measurements and inspect the finished container label.

Evidence and feedback: The assessor observes the task and checks whether the learner: measures accurately, labels appropriately and selects controls for splash and inhalation exposure. A learner must explain any unsafe choice, correct it and repeat the demonstration. Record observations, required coaching and reassessment rather than awarding competence from attendance alone.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Check the job scope, site instructions, manufacturer directions and your training before mixing or applying any product.
Read the manufacturer's dilution instructions on the product label and measure using a dedicated, labelled measuring system; this lesson gives no dilution ratios.
Never estimate concentration by colour or smell, and do not strengthen a mix on the view that it will work better.
Assess ventilation, splashing, aerosols and nearby people before application.
Wear the PPE specified for the product and the task.
If the surface, the soil or hazard, or the approved method is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Dilution is measured against the manufacturer's directions using a dedicated, labelled measuring system.
Concentration is never estimated by colour or smell.
Ventilation, splashing, aerosols and nearby people are assessed before application.
Finished containers are labelled, and splash and inhalation controls suit the product and task.
summary: Dilution follows the manufacturer's instructions, is measured with a dedicated and labelled system, and is never estimated by colour or smell.
Ventilation, splashing, aerosols and nearby people are assessed before any product is applied.
A stronger mix is not treated as more effective, and the PPE specified for the product and task is worn.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you check before performing dilution, ventilation and exposure controls?
options: The manufacturer's dilution instructions, plus the ventilation, splash risk and people nearby
How the concentrate looks in the bottle on the shelf, the label and the lid
Whether a stronger mix will work faster on the stain, the room and the surface
How strong the smell is, as a guide to the dilution needed for the job and the room

knowledgeChecks.question: What do you do when the correct dilution of a product is unclear?
options: Double the concentrate to be sure the soil lifts off the surface
Estimate the strength by eye and keep going on the job today
Keep working and adjust the mix as you go along the whole job
Pause and seek supervisor guidance on the approved dilution before going on

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the lesson say concentration must be set?
options: By eye, using the strongest mix
By the manufacturer's dilution instructions and a dedicated labelled measuring system
By whatever the last job used
